---
title: "HTML, slides, and dashboards"
---

## HTML pages

In HTML, a wrapped figure floats to its side, and the paragraphs after it
flow beside it. In a window as wide as the
[breakpoint](../defaults.qmd#breakpoint) or narrower, figures stop floating
and take the full width of the text column. A width or gap can be a CSS
length, a percent, or a [CSS function](../width-gap.qmd#css-functions-in-html).

A figure in the margin, a figure with its caption in the margin, and a
figure in a page-wide column keep their normal layout in HTML. [Where a
figure keeps its normal layout](../normal-layout.qmd) gives the full list.

## Slides

In revealjs slides, a wrapped figure floats beside the paragraphs after it
on the same slide, as on an HTML page:

```markdown
## Results

![Mean ratings by condition.](ratings.png){#fig-ratings .wrap-right width="40%"}

Ratings rose in both conditions.
```

Slides have no margin column, no margin captions, and no page-wide
columns. A figure with a margin caption or a page-wide class still wraps on
a slide. A margin setting does not stop a figure from wrapping on a slide
either: a `.column-margin` or `.fig-column-margin` class, a `.column-margin`
div, a code cell with `#| column: margin` or `#| fig-column: margin`, or
`fig-column: margin` or `column: margin` in the document metadata.

By default, revealjs puts an `.aside` div at the foot of the slide. A
figure in an aside div does not wrap. It keeps its normal layout, and the
render prints one warning for it.

## Dashboards

In a dashboard (`format: dashboard`), a wrapped figure in a `.card` div
floats beside the paragraphs after it in that card. So does an image in
the card that Quarto makes for the text of a row or a column.
Code cell figures are tested with knitr cells that make one plot.

In a row or a column, Quarto makes a code cell outside a `.card` div into
a card of its own. The paragraphs after the cell are then in another
card. So a figure from any code cell outside a `.card` div keeps its
normal layout. The render prints one warning for it, or one for a cell
that makes more than one figure. To wrap the figure, put the cell and its
paragraphs in a `.card` div:

````markdown
::: {.card title="Ratings"}

::: {.cell .wrap-right}

```{.r .cell-code}
plot(1:10)
```

::: {.cell-output-display}
![Mean ratings by condition.](html_files/figure-html/fig-ratings-1.png){#fig-ratings width=40%}
:::
:::


Ratings rose in both conditions.
:::
````

Sidebars, tabsets, value boxes, and card toolbars are not tested.
